comparator.name: Bachelor Theology
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page and 2026-2027 study guide identify a three-year, 180-EC Bachelor Theology. The programme is a broad confessional-Reformed theology degree spanning biblical studies and exegesis, systematic theology and ethics, church and theology history, practical theology, missiology, philosophy and religious studies. Biblical Greek and Hebrew continue across the curriculum, while personal and professional formation, academic skills, integration work and practice connect scholarship to church and society. The third year includes advanced theological subjects, choice or minor space and a 10-EC Bachelor thesis. The optional Bible Translation route is not selected for this generic normalized target; the ordinary broad theology curriculum is reconstructed instead.
components: Year 1: theological, biblical-language and academic foundations

Foundations in theology and prolegomena, academic skills, biblical Greek and Hebrew, church history, philosophy, the formation of the Bible, introductory exegesis and biblical-context study, personal and professional formation, and integration activities.
Year 2: disciplinary theology, exegesis and church practice

Progression in biblical Greek and Hebrew, Old and New Testament exegesis and theology, Christian ethics, doctrine, hermeneutics, church history, practical theology, mission, worship and preaching, with continuing formation and integration work.
Year 3: advanced theology, choice space and Bachelor thesis

Advanced biblical, systematic, historical and practical theology; continuing biblical languages; church history, ecumenics and world religions; homiletics and liturgy; elective or minor space; and the 10-EC Bachelor thesis with methodology.

exception.reason: The TUA Bachelor Theology is a cumulative confessional-Reformed theology degree. Its academic identity depends on sustained biblical Greek and Hebrew, Old and New Testament exegesis, biblical hermeneutics, systematic and doctrinal theology, Christian ethics, church and theology history, practical theology, missiology, homiletics, liturgy, pastoral and professional formation, and a theology-specific Bachelor thesis. UCR offers adjacent work in philosophy, ethics, history, literature, rhetoric, sociology, politics and cultural study, but it offers no academic theology or religious-studies curriculum, no biblical-language or exegesis sequence, and no practical-theology or church-practice formation. A 24-course UCR pathway could examine ideas, texts, history and society, but it could not preserve the target programme's defining theological formation.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official sources account for the complete 180 EC as three 60-EC years. Year 1 establishes theology, academic skills, biblical languages, church history and biblical-text foundations. Year 2 advances biblical languages, exegesis, hermeneutics, doctrine, Christian ethics, church history, practical theology and mission. Year 3 combines advanced biblical, systematic, historical and practical theology with continuing languages, choice or minor space and a 10-EC Bachelor thesis. The official programme explicitly describes the degree as broad theology taught from a confessional-Reformed perspective and integrates scholarship, church practice and personal formation throughout. The optional Bible Translation route does not alter the ordinary programme's central theological and biblical-language spine and is not selected here.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy, GOSPHIL212 Ethics, GOSPOLI111 Introduction to Political Philosophy and GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy support philosophical and moral inquiry. GOSHIST111 Modern History, the wider history sequence, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature provide historical, literary and mythological context; MCCCOMM111 The Art of Rhetorical Communication supports textual and persuasive analysis; and sociology and politics courses can examine institutions and public life. The workbook nevertheless contains no theology or religious-studies course, biblical studies, Old or New Testament exegesis, hermeneutics of scripture, biblical Greek, Hebrew or Aramaic, systematic theology or dogmatics, church history as a disciplinary sequence, missiology, ecclesiology, practical theology, homiletics, liturgy, pastoral care, or theology-specific research project. The adjacent humanities and social-science courses address different objects and methods and cannot substitute for the connected theological, linguistic, exegetical and professional formation required by the TUA degree.
